<a id="letter-a"></a>

## A

<a id="abstraction"></a>**Abstraction** — A simplified description of a system level that exposes a contract (inputs, outputs, assumptions) and hides internal detail, so that the level above can be designed without the detail. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="ac-analysis"></a>**AC analysis** — A simulation of a circuit's small-signal sinusoidal response versus frequency, computed with phasors after linearizing around the operating point. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="activity-factor"></a>**Activity factor** — α, the fraction of clock cycles in which a node makes a 0→1 transition; it scales the dynamic power αCV²f. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="adiabatic-charging"></a>**Adiabatic charging** — Charging a capacitor with a slowly ramped or stepped source so that the voltage across the series resistance stays small, reducing the loss below ½CV² (to CV²/2N for N equal steps). *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="angle-argument"></a>**Angle (argument)** — The direction ∠z of a complex number's arrow, measured counterclockwise from the positive real axis; computed with the quadrant-aware atan2(y, x). This curriculum reports principal values in (−180°, 180°]. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="angular-frequency"></a>**Angular frequency** — ω = 2πf, the rate of a sinusoid's phase advance in rad/s, where f is the frequency in hertz. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="letter-c"></a>

## C

<a id="catastrophic-cancellation"></a>**Catastrophic cancellation** — The loss of significant digits when subtracting two nearly equal floating-point numbers; avoided by algebraic rearrangement or series expansion. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="characteristic-impedance"></a>**Characteristic impedance** — Z0, the ratio of voltage to current for a single wave traveling along a transmission line (typically 50 Ω for coaxial cable and RF systems). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="chiplet"></a>**Chiplet** — A die designed to be combined with other dies inside one package, so that a system can exceed the reticle limit or mix processes; chiplets communicate over die-to-die links. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="complex-conjugate"></a>**Complex conjugate** — For z = x + jy, the number z\* = x − jy, its mirror image across the real axis. z z\* = |z|², which is why conjugates are used to divide complex numbers. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-exponential"></a>**Complex exponential** — A signal e^{st} with complex s = σ + jω. It rotates at ω rad/s while its magnitude grows (σ > 0), decays (σ < 0) or stays constant (σ = 0); its real part is a growing, decaying or steady sinusoid. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-number"></a>**Complex number** — A number z = x + jy with real part x and imaginary part y (both real numbers), drawn as a point or arrow in the complex plane. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Imaginary unit](#imaginary-unit), [Complex plane](#complex-plane).

<a id="complex-plane"></a>**Complex plane** — The plane in which a complex number x + jy is plotted at horizontal coordinate x (real axis) and vertical coordinate y (imaginary axis). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="continuity-of-capacitor-voltage-and-inductor-current"></a>**Continuity of capacitor voltage and inductor current** — The rule that v_C and i_L cannot change instantaneously (it would take infinite current or voltage, and infinite power). Other circuit variables can jump at switching instants. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="convolution"></a>**Convolution** — The operation y(t) = ∫ h(t−λ) u(λ) dλ that gives a linear time-invariant system's output from its input and impulse response; for a first-order low-pass, an exponentially weighted average of past inputs. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="corner-frequency"></a>**Corner frequency** — For a single-pole response H = 1/(1 + jωτ), the frequency ω = 1/τ where |H| = 1/√2 (−3 dB) and the phase is −45°; commonly used to define bandwidth. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="letter-d"></a>

## D

<a id="de-moivres-theorem"></a>**De Moivre's theorem** — (r∠θ)ⁿ = rⁿ∠nθ. Raising a complex number to a power raises its magnitude to that power and multiplies its angle. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="dynamic-power"></a>**Dynamic power** — Power consumed by charging and discharging capacitances in switching circuits, P = αCV²f, independent of the resistance of the charging path. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Activity factor](#activity-factor).

<a id="letter-e"></a>

## E

<a id="electronic-design-automation-eda"></a>**Electronic design automation (EDA)** — The software used to design and verify chips and boards, covering simulation, synthesis, place-and-route, timing and verification; dominated commercially by Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="error-vector-magnitude"></a>**Error vector magnitude** — EVM, the RMS distance between transmitted (or received) constellation points and their ideal positions, relative to the signal, often quoted in dB. It sets the highest usable QAM order. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="eulers-formula"></a>**Euler's formula** — e^{jθ} = cos θ + j sin θ for real θ. It connects exponentials and sinusoids and makes r∠θ and re^{jθ} the same number. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="letter-f"></a>

## F

<a id="first-order-circuit"></a>**First-order circuit** — A circuit whose behavior is described by a first-order differential equation, typically one with a single (equivalent) capacitor or inductor. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="flyback-diode"></a>**Flyback diode** — A diode placed across an inductive load so that, when the driving switch opens, the inductor's current circulates through the diode, clamping the switch voltage to about one diode drop above the supply. Also called a freewheeling diode. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="formal-verification"></a>**Formal verification** — Using mathematical proof (model checking, equivalence checking) to show that a design satisfies a property for all possible inputs, instead of testing examples. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="frequency-response"></a>**Frequency response** — The complex gain H(jω) of a linear system at angular frequency ω. Its magnitude scales a sinusoid's amplitude and its angle shifts the sinusoid's phase. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Corner frequency](#corner-frequency).

<a id="functional-coverage"></a>**Functional coverage** — A measure of which specified behaviors, input combinations or corner cases a verification run has actually exercised; used to decide when verification is complete. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="letter-h"></a>

## H

<a id="hardware-description-language-hdl"></a>**Hardware description language (HDL)** — A language such as Verilog, SystemVerilog or VHDL for describing digital hardware structure and behavior, used for simulation and synthesis. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="letter-i"></a>

## I

<a id="iq"></a>**I/Q (in-phase/quadrature)** — Representation of a bandpass signal by two baseband components, in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q), which together form one complex sample stream I + jQ; the native signal format of modern radios. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Error vector magnitude](#error-vector-magnitude).

<a id="imaginary-unit"></a>**Imaginary unit** — The number j defined by j² = −1 (written i in mathematics; EE uses j because i denotes current). Multiplying by j rotates a complex number 90° counterclockwise. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="impedance"></a>**Impedance** — The ratio Z = V/I of voltage phasor to current phasor for an element or network, in ohms. Resistor R, inductor jωL, capacitor 1/(jωC). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Reactance](#reactance), [Phasor](#phasor).

<a id="inductive-kick"></a>**Inductive kick** — The large voltage an inductor develops (v = L di/dt) when its current is interrupted abruptly; it can arc switch contacts or break down transistors unless a flyback path is provided. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Flyback diode](#flyback-diode).

<a id="instruction-set-architecture-isa"></a>**Instruction-set architecture (ISA)** — The contract between hardware and software, namely the instructions, registers, memory model and exceptions a program can rely on, independent of how a processor implements them. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="integrating-factor"></a>**Integrating factor** — A multiplier (e^{t/τ} for τ x' + x = u) that turns the left side of a first-order linear ODE into an exact derivative, giving the general solution as an integral of the input. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="integrator-op-amp"></a>**Integrator (op-amp)** — An op-amp circuit with a capacitor in the feedback path and a resistor at the input, giving v_out = −(1/RC)∫v_in dt; a resistor across the capacitor makes it a "leaky" integrator (a first-order low-pass). *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="letter-k"></a>

## K

<a id="ktc-noise"></a>**kT/C noise** — The thermal noise sampled onto a capacitor through any resistance, with RMS value √(kT/C), about 64 µV for 1 pF at 300 K; independent of the resistance. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="letter-l"></a>

## L

<a id="least-significant-bit-lsb"></a>**Least significant bit (LSB)** — The smallest step an N-bit converter resolves, full scale / 2^N; errors and noise are often expressed in LSBs. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="level-shifter"></a>**Level shifter** — A circuit that translates logic levels between two voltage domains so that families with incompatible thresholds can communicate. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="lumped-matter-discipline"></a>**Lumped-matter discipline** — The conditions under which fields can be replaced by voltages and currents in lumped elements obeying KVL and KCL, chiefly that the circuit is small compared with the signal wavelength (or line delay is short compared with edge time). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Transmission line](#transmission-line), [Wavelength](#wavelength).

<a id="letter-m"></a>

## M

<a id="machine-epsilon"></a>**Machine epsilon** — The gap between 1 and the next representable floating-point number, 2^−52 ≈ 2.22×10^−16 for IEEE 754 double precision; the relative precision of a computation. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="magnitude"></a>**Magnitude** — The length |z| = √(x² + y²) of a complex number's arrow (also called modulus or absolute value). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="modified-nodal-analysis"></a>**Modified nodal analysis** — The formulation SPICE uses, namely KCL at every node plus extra equations for voltage sources, giving a linear system G·v = i (re-linearized each iteration for nonlinear devices). *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="letter-n"></a>

## N

<a id="natural-response"></a>**Natural response** — The response of a circuit with no sources acting, driven only by the energy initially stored in its capacitors and inductors; for a first-order circuit, an exponential decay. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="netlist"></a>**Netlist** — A text description of a circuit listing each element, its value and the nodes it connects; the input to a circuit simulator (node 0 is ground). *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="newton-raphson-method"></a>**Newton–Raphson method** — An iterative root-finding method, x_{k+1} = x_k − g(x_k)/g′(x_k), that circuit simulators use to solve nonlinear equations; it converges quadratically near a solution but can overshoot far from it. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="noise-margin"></a>**Noise margin** — The amount of noise a digital connection can tolerate, NM_L = V_IL − V_OL and NM_H = V_OH − V_IH. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="letter-o"></a>

## O

<a id="operating-point"></a>**Operating point** — The DC voltages and currents of a circuit with its sources at their DC values (capacitors open, inductors shorted); also called the bias point. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="letter-p"></a>

## P

<a id="phase"></a>**Phase** — The angle φ in A cos(ωt + φ), fixing where in its cycle a sinusoid is at t = 0. A time delay t_d is a phase lag of ωt_d. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="phasor"></a>**Phasor** — The complex number V = V_m∠φ representing the sinusoid V_m cos(ωt + φ) at a known frequency ω, so that v(t) = Re{V e^{jωt}}. This curriculum uses peak-amplitude, cosine-reference phasors. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Sinusoidal steady state](#sinusoidal-steady-state), [Impedance](#impedance).

<a id="polar-form"></a>**Polar form** — Writing a complex number by its magnitude and angle, z = r∠θ = r(cos θ + j sin θ) = re^{jθ}. Convenient for multiplication, division, powers and roots. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Rectangular form](#rectangular-form), [Euler's formula](#eulers-formula).

<a id="process-design-kit-pdk"></a>**Process design kit (PDK)** — The files a foundry gives designers to use its process, including device models, design rules, layer definitions and often standard-cell libraries, abstracting the fab's recipes. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="propagation-delay"></a>**Propagation delay** — The time from an input transition to the output crossing 50 % of its swing; for an RC model, τ·ln 2 ≈ 0.69τ. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="letter-q"></a>

## Q

<a id="q-function"></a>**Q-function** — Q(x), the probability that a standard normal random variable exceeds x; it gives error probabilities for decisions in Gaussian noise and falls off extremely fast (Q(6) ≈ 1e-9). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="letter-r"></a>

## R

<a id="reactance"></a>**Reactance** — The imaginary part X of an impedance Z = R + jX, in ohms. Positive for inductors (ωL), negative for capacitors (−1/(ωC)). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="rectangular-form"></a>**Rectangular form** — Writing a complex number by its components, z = x + jy. Convenient for addition and subtraction. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Polar form](#polar-form).

<a id="reflection-coefficient"></a>**Reflection coefficient** — Γ = (R − Z0)/(R + Z0), the ratio of reflected to incident wave voltage at a termination R on a line of characteristic impedance Z0; +1 for an open, −1 for a short, 0 for a matched load. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="regeneration"></a>**Regeneration** — Restoring a signal to clean logic levels at each stage, so that noise does not accumulate along a chain; the key advantage of digital over analog processing. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="repeater"></a>**Repeater** — A buffer inserted along a long on-chip wire to break it into shorter segments, converting delay that grows with the square of length into delay that grows linearly. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="resonance"></a>**Resonance** — The condition in an LC-containing circuit where inductive and capacitive reactances cancel (ω₀ = 1/√(LC) in a series RLC), making the impedance purely resistive and the response peak. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="reticle-limit"></a>**Reticle limit** — The largest area one lithography exposure can print, 26 mm × 33 mm ≈ 858 mm² on standard scanners (half that with High-NA EUV); it caps the size of a single die without stitching. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Chiplet](#chiplet).

<a id="rise-time"></a>**Rise time** — The time a response takes to go from 10 % to 90 % of its total change; τ·ln 9 ≈ 2.2τ for a single pole, so t_r ≈ 0.35/f_3dB. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="rms-value"></a>**RMS value** — Root-mean-square value, √(average of v²). For a sinusoid of amplitude V_m it is V_m/√2; it is the value that delivers the same average power to a resistor as a DC voltage of that size. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="roots-of-unity"></a>**Roots of unity** — The N complex numbers e^{j2πk/N} (k = 0 … N−1) whose N-th power is 1, equally spaced on the unit circle. They are the twiddle factors of the FFT. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="letter-s"></a>

## S

<a id="sample-and-hold"></a>**Sample-and-hold** — A circuit that connects a capacitor to a signal through a switch (sample), then disconnects it to hold the voltage while it is converted; its settling and kT/C noise limit ADC accuracy. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="self-checking-testbench"></a>**Self-checking testbench** — A testbench that compares the design's outputs with independently computed expected values and reports pass or fail automatically, rather than relying on a human reading waveforms. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="settling-time"></a>**Settling time** — The time a response takes to come and stay within a specified error band of its final value; τ·ln(1/ε) for a first-order system, and (N+1)·ln 2 · τ to reach ½ LSB of an N-bit converter. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="side-channel"></a>**Side channel** — An unintended leak of information through physical behavior such as timing, power consumption or electromagnetic emission, which can reveal secrets that the logical abstraction hides. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="sinusoid"></a>**Sinusoid** — A signal of the form A cos(ωt + φ), with amplitude A, angular frequency ω and phase φ. This curriculum always uses the cosine as the reference form. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="sinusoidal-steady-state"></a>**Sinusoidal steady state** — The response of a stable linear system to a sinusoidal input after transients have died out, a sinusoid at the input frequency whose amplitude and phase follow from phasor analysis. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="spice"></a>**SPICE** — Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis, the standard family of circuit simulators that solve a netlist's nodal equations for DC, AC and transient behavior; ngspice is an open-source version. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md). *See also:* [Netlist](#netlist), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="state-variable"></a>**State variable** — A variable that fully captures a circuit's stored energy and memory, namely capacitor voltages and inductor currents. Knowing them at one instant (plus the inputs) determines the future response. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="static-discipline"></a>**Static discipline** — The rule defining valid digital levels with separate output (V_OL, V_OH) and input (V_IL, V_IH) thresholds, so that every gate restores clean levels and leaves noise margins. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Noise margin](#noise-margin).

<a id="step-response"></a>**Step response** — The response of a circuit to a source that switches from one constant value to another; for a first-order circuit, an exponential approach to the new final value. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="letter-t"></a>

## T

<a id="testbench"></a>**Testbench** — Simulation-only code that instantiates a design, applies inputs and checks outputs; the executable form of a design's specification. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md). *See also:* [Self-checking testbench](#self-checking-testbench).

<a id="thevenin-resistance"></a>**Thevenin resistance** — R_Th, the resistance seen looking into two terminals of a linear circuit with its independent sources turned off; it sets the time constant seen by a capacitor or inductor connected there. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="time-constant"></a>**Time constant** — τ, the characteristic time of a first-order exponential response e^{−t/τ}; τ = R_Th·C for an RC circuit and τ = L/R_Th for an RL circuit. After one τ, 63.2 % of the change is complete. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Thevenin resistance](#thevenin-resistance), [Settling time](#settling-time).

<a id="transient"></a>**Transient** — The part of a circuit's response that dies out after a disturbance (such as a switching event), as the circuit moves from one steady state to another. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Time constant](#time-constant).

<a id="transient-analysis"></a>**Transient analysis** — A simulation of a circuit's voltages and currents versus time for arbitrary input waveforms, computed step by step with numerical integration. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="transmission-line"></a>**Transmission line** — A pair of conductors along which signals travel as waves with finite speed, so that voltage and current vary with position and reflections occur at impedance changes. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Characteristic impedance](#characteristic-impedance), [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="letter-w"></a>

## W

<a id="wavelength"></a>**Wavelength** — The distance λ = v/f a wave travels in one period, where v is the propagation speed and f the frequency. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).
